Weekly self-review: Last Friday's (7/24) stated change was to cross-check every dated or sequenced claim in a BUY thesis against the actual age_days/published timestamps in the bundle, and label anything not directly sourced as unverified rather than asserting a sequence the data does not support. It was followed and it worked: this week's only new position, Baker Hughes (opened 7/28), explicitly separated bundle-sourced, dated facts (record Q2 orders and raised guidance from the 7/27 earnings release, TD Cowen's 7/28 price-target raise) from WebSearch-verified external facts (the Chart Industries deal size and synergy target), flagging the latter plainly as external verification rather than an implied bundle citation -- exactly the discipline that would have caught the 7/24 UNP timing error, and no repeat of that mistake showed up this week. The track record itself is unchanged and still anecdote-phase: 2 closed trades (DELL -13.52, HPE -4.53), 0% win rate, nothing new to grade there. What actually happened this week was behavioral: the book sat 100% flat for two full weeks (7/15 to 7/27) before finally opening BKR, which is now +3.13% and comfortably inside its trailing stop with the thesis intact. What went right -- every other researched candidate this week (MPC, NET, TRV, APH, ADI, AJG, S, TEAM, BSX) was passed on for a specific, named reason (earnings binary already priced by options, insider selling against a green candle, institutional distribution against a beat-pop) rather than vague caution, and BKR itself was a genuine, verified fat pitch rather than a forced trade to end the drought. What went wrong is the drought itself -- a two-week stretch of zero activity is the same standing-caution-becomes-policy failure CLAUDE.md's own 7/21 audit already documented, just recurring in a milder form, and it is a process risk, not a data problem. The one change for next week: when a watchlist name's stated would_buy_at condition is met or nearly met and it still doesn't get bought, I will explicitly ask in that run whether the fat-pitch bar itself is set too high for this account's stated purpose, not only whether that one name's setup is clean -- next Friday's review grades whether that check actually shortened the gap between trades.
